topics.title: The $1.5B author settlement just got thrown out — and a new judge inherits the mess
topics.why: A judge rejected Anthropic's record copyright settlement over fairness concerns and a new judge just took the case, so the ruling that will decide whether AI vendors can legally train on copyrighted work is back in play.

topics.title: Congress wants veto power over your next GPU order
topics.why: A House committee voted 42-2 to advance a bill banning Blackwell-class chip sales to China and giving Congress a say over AI chip export licenses, which is already rippling into cloud GPU pricing.

topics.title: The hidden gig economy training your chatbot has a name, and it's hiring
topics.why: Platforms like Outlier, DataAnnotation, and Mercor — plus Uber's new in-house data-labeling division — are quietly running a real side-income lane most knowledge workers have never heard of.

topics.title: 2026 was supposed to be the year enterprise AI 'just worked.' It isn't, yet.
topics.why: OpenAI's own CFO called 2026 the year of practical adoption, but fresh reliability and hallucination audits are the real reason some rollouts are stalling — a useful reality check for anyone buying or deploying these tools.

topics.title: Humanoid robots just got a real hiring pipeline
topics.why: BMW, Hyundai, and Siemens are now running humanoid robots on actual factory floors at meaningful scale, and the skills gap it's creating (robot supervision, physical-AI integration) is a distinct career lane from the software-agent story.
